white.frontSub: Jaw loose, feet down, name the feeling · Style, blind spot, or tactic? · Proposal, then stop.
white.backSub: If the honest answer is no, you are not asking—you are pressuring. (Sanctuary check: "Am I here, and are they?")

blue.front: Baseline first. Name the need, not the position. Label, then pause.
blue.frontSub: 60s sweep + camera test; check your own tells first · Honor the concern or fear at zero cost; hold your boundary · Drop 'I', name it lightly, hold 3 seconds of silence

brown.frontSub: Brown Belt Pocket Card Close Tap the card to turn it over. Three cues for visibility, syntax, and transparent steering. 1. Frame before you ask. Name the purpose first; wrap the face-threat without swallowing the ask. 2. Say what you want, once. Advocate before you inquire; strip powerless hedges. 3. Steer out loud. Name the decision type (inform, consult, negotiate) and invite choice. Brown Belt Core Question “What reality are my words building?” Every turn carries a message and a metamessage. Choose both on purpose.
brown.back: What reality are my words building?

black.front: 1. Read the room before the person. · 2. Name the pattern, not the person. · 3. Offer a better game.
black.back: Am I a bridge here, or a code-switcher?

sanctuary.front: Am I here, and are they?
sanctuary.back: Am I here, and are they?

stages.t: Opportunist · unilateral power · Bridges ≈ Denial / Defense
stages.gift: Spots threats and leverage instantly; refuses to be a doormat.
stages.shadow: Sees every friction as an attack; counter-manipulates or explodes.
stages.tell: Snapping back, issuing ultimatums, keeping score.
stages.move: Run W1 2-beat exhale and W4 triage before reacting.

stages.t: Diplomat · referent power · Bridges ≈ Defense / Minimization
stages.gift: Reads social mood fast; preserves surface harmony.
stages.shadow: Apologizes while someone crosses their line; offers Reason #2 out of guilt.
stages.tell: "Sorry to bother you, I just wanted to check if maybe…"
stages.move: Deliver one W5 Clean No with zero apologies and hold the 5-second aftermath.

stages.gift: Catches inconsistencies and logical flaws rapidly.
stages.shadow: Over-explains to prove intelligence; debates bad-faith pushers.
stages.tell: Three paragraphs of justification when one sentence would do.
stages.move: Cap explanations at one factual reason; switch to W6 Fog + Broken Record.

stages.t: Achiever · productive power · Bridges ≈ Minimization / Acceptance
stages.gift: Sets clear deliverables, timelines, and written records.
stages.shadow: Treats personal boundaries like cold transactions; over-functions.
stages.tell: Fixing or project-managing instead of feeling anger or hurt.
stages.move: Name the feeling silently (W1 Step 2) and add warmth in personal boundaries.

stages.gift: Sees the human story behind difficult behavior.
stages.shadow: Over-understands; excuses repeated violations; Observer withdrawal.
stages.tell: "From where they stand, it makes sense why they pushed."
stages.move: Run Simon's Cut-Off Question: understand the motive, still judge the behavior.

stages.t: Strategist · transforming, mutual power · Bridges ≈ Adaptation
stages.gift: Triages style vs. blind spot vs. tactic; holds boundaries calmly without blame.
stages.shadow: Whitewashing own fallbacks or over-naming dynamics too soon.
stages.tell: "What's really happening here, and what do I want from it?"
stages.move: Answer BOTH halves of the Strategist sentence and honor the 3-line confirming email.

stages.gift: Sees manipulation as a game without getting hooked; stays grounded.
stages.shadow: Detachment that misses real danger or delays a needed boundary.
stages.tell: Calm amusement while a real limit is being crossed.
stages.move: Keep Safety Rule #9 and a concrete protective consequence bolted to the floor.

read: Reads for advantage
Quick to spot threats and openings.
Reads people only for what can be taken or defended.
Inner question: what can I get here?
Notice one need someone has that does nothing for you.
Torbert pp. 66–68
bond: Affection as currency; drops people once they are used.
Do one kindness with no return expected.

read: Reads for approval
Fast at sensing mood and approval in the room.
Reads to avoid friction; mistakes politeness for agreement.
Inner question: are they upset with me?
Name what they need, not what they think of you.
Torbert pp. 68–76; Hughes needs map
bond: Bonds by agreeing; can't stay close through conflict.
Disagree on something small and stay warm.

read: Reads for errors
Precise: catches inconsistencies, fallacies, verbal leakage.
Reads content, not need; diagnoses people; blind to the emotional room.
Tracks what's wrong with what was just said.
Assume everyone has something to teach you. For every flaw you spot, find one need.
Torbert pp. 78–84; Hughes verbal indicators
bond: Deep bonds with people who share a discipline.
Respect gated by competence; corrects instead of connects.
Ask about their experience before offering your knowledge.

read: Reads for interests
Reads goals, interests and decision drivers; spots the path to yes.
Instrumental: the person becomes a means to the outcome.
Inner question: what will get them to agree?
Read one thing about them that has nothing to do with your goal.
Torbert pp. 81–86; Hughes pp. 200–203
bond: Relationships managed like projects; dropped when goals diverge.
Spend time with someone with no agenda at all.

read: Reads their frame
Reads each person's model of reality from inside it.
Over-understands: explains away behavior by understanding motives.
Inner sentence: from where they stand, it makes sense.
After you understand the motive, still judge the behavior.
Torbert pp. 91–103; Brooks pp. 147–149; Simon p. 96
bond: Makes people feel understood across difference.
Empathy without boundaries; gives understanding, asks for nothing back.
Loop for understanding, then share your own reaction.

read: Reads the system
Reads the pattern between people, the threatened core concern, the real conversation type, and self in real time.
Reads more than others want named; assumes they are ready for it.
Said aloud: I think this is a status conversation, not a money one.
Name the dynamic tentatively and invite correction.
Torbert pp. 22–27, 104–111; Duhigg p. 246
bond: Stays close through conflict; repairs ruptures.
May push intimacy faster than others can hold.
I disagree, and I'm not going anywhere.
Name the rupture and invite repair.

read: Reads the reading itself
Sees how expectation and projection shape every read, including your own.
Infinite regress: trusts no read enough to act on it.
Inner sentence: notice what I am assuming about you.
Hold the read lightly and loop it back to them to check.
Torbert pp. 177–193; Duhigg pp. 303–309
bond: Meets the person underneath identities and roles.
Comfortable silences; few words, full attention.

cols.q: What is actually happening, in them, in me, between us?

word: Words as weapons
Direct, blunt, cuts through ambiguity.
Bald on-record demands; blames or coerces.
Tell: 'Take it or leave it.'
Move: State a clear ask without threat or sting.
reveal: False front
Confident exterior under pressure.
Reveals strategically as bait; overshares to create obligation.
Tell: Calculated charm before a lopsided ask.
Move: Share one small, plain truth with zero hook attached.
steer: Steers by force
Decisive in genuine emergencies.
Imposes unilateral direction; treats pushback as betrayal.
Tell: Ultimatums and artificial urgency.
Move: Name the decision type (inform/consult/negotiate) out loud.

word: Words to keep peace
Warm, tactful, protects group harmony.
Hedged, apologetic asks from below; softens until the ask vanishes.
Tell: 'Sorry to bother you, just checking if maybe…'
Move: Strip powerless hedges and state the ask once.
reveal: Edited self
Considerate of what the room can hold.
Hides true needs, objections, and preferences to avoid friction.
Tell: 'I'm fine with whatever works for everyone.'
Move: State one honest preference first before asking theirs.
steer: Follows the room
Reliable team glue; honors norms.
Abdicates direction; lets others set the frame silently.
Tell: Waits to be approached or invited to speak.
Move: Open one meeting or plan by naming the purpose first.

word: Words to prove right
Precise, rigorous, airtight craft language.
Precision used to win; over-explains until unassailable.
Tell: 'Actually, technically…' + 3 extra paragraphs.
Move: Frame and advocate in 2 sentences; stop before lecturing.
reveal: Reveals knowledge, not self
Generous with expertise and analysis.
Facts instead of feelings; credentials as armor.
Tell: Answers a personal question with a framework.
Move: Drop the credentials and name one real personal stake.
steer: Steers by winning the argument
Strong logical structure and standards.
Debates details while missing relational or political frames.
Tell: Floods the table with data when challenged.
Move: Pair one data point with a genuine inquiry into their frame.

word: Words to close the deal
Clear, goal-oriented, compelling.
Achiever's Spin: partnership language hiding a unilateral funnel.
Tell: 'In the spirit of partnership, let's lock this by 5.'
Move: Separate message from metamessage; invite real dissent.
reveal: The résumé self
Articulates goals, wins, and accountability.
Hides uncertainty, fatigue, or unfinished edges.
Tell: 'Crushing it, busy, all good!'
Move: Offer one processed vulnerability without spinning it as a win.
steer: Steers to the deal
Moves groups reliably toward outcomes.
Treats conversations as projects to close rather than mutual choices.
Tell: Rushes past emotional/social lanes to next steps.
Move: Ask a calibrated question that hands real agency back.

word: Words that hold nuance
Attentive to context, voice, and subtext.
Over-qualifies; hedges until nobody knows what was asked.
Tell: 'On the one hand… though I also see…'
Move: Advocate your actual view plainly after naming context.
reveal: Authentic, sometimes unedited
Honest about inner tension and values.
Asks brilliant questions while hiding own position (Pluralist question trap).
Tell: 5 deep questions in a row, zero self-advocacy.
Move: Use all 4 parts of speech: frame and advocate before inquiring.
steer: Hesitates to steer
Respects every voice and perspective.
Avoids taking the wheel for fear of imposing; lets talks drift.
Tell: 'What do you all think we should do?' (no proposal).
Move: Propose one clear direction openly and invite edits.

word: Words that build shared reality
Names purpose, aligns message and metamessage across dialects.
Unspoken frame control slides into manipulation.
Tell: 'I'd like to frame our goal for the next 20 minutes…'
Move: Run the 3-culture Translation Strip; keep framing transparent.
reveal: Calibrated, grounded visibility
Uses Torbert's 4 parts cleanly; owns flaws without groveling.
Disclosure that overwhelms people who aren't ready (or whitewashing).
Tell: Plain stake + concrete example + open inquiry.
Move: Match disclosure size to consent and room readiness.
steer: Steers out loud with others
Transparent direction; names inform/consult/negotiate cleanly.
Overestimates others' readiness for meta-steering.
Tell: 'I'd like to steer us toward X. Does that work for you?'
Move: Confirm their yes/no honestly (White Belt check).

word: Words held lightly as maps
Hears borrowed voices, language games, and silence.
Abstraction that leaves practical teammates stranded.
Tell: 'Notice how the words we're using frame this as a fight.'
Move: Pair any linguistic reframe with one concrete next step.
reveal: Unarmored presence
Drops performance; meets others as still becoming.
Detachment that can feel unreachable or evasive.
Tell: Quiet candor without defending an image.
Move: Anchor multi-perspectival insight in one clear commitment.
steer: Changes what it is about
Dissolves binary deadlocks by shifting the premise.
Reframes to avoid a concrete decision someone needs.
Tell: 'Maybe the real question isn't A or B…'
Move: After reframing, land one concrete next step.
Steers by force
Decisive in genuine emergencies.
Imposes unilateral direction; treats pushback as betrayal.
Tell: Ultimatums and rigged urgency.
Move: Name the game fairly; offer one transparent choice.
guard: Guards by striking first
Spots threats and leverage instantly.
Sees every room as hostile; counter-manipulates to win.
Tell: Retaliation disguised as self-defense.
Move: Drop the rope on one petty power play without striking back.
bridges: Denial / Defense (Room Analogy)
Clear loyalty to own group's survival.
Us-vs.-them polarity; difference feels like threat.
Tell: 'Our way works; theirs is broken.'
Move: Notice one legitimate concern inside the opposing tribe.

steer: Follows the room
Protects harmony and group cohesion.
Abdicates frame; lets louder voices steer silently.
Tell: 'Whatever works for everyone.'
Move: Name one shared goal out loud before the room drifts.
guard: Guards by appeasing
Reads social weather fast to prevent blows.
Tolerates covert tactics to keep the peace; over-accommodates.
Tell: Apologizing when someone else crosses your line.
Move: Hold one clean boundary without softening it with Reason #2.
bridges: Defense / Minimization (Room Analogy)
Warmth and search for common ground.
Code-switches until the self disappears; flattens real difference.
Tell: 'We're all basically the same here.'
Move: Drop one reflexive translation tax this week.

steer: Steers by winning the argument
Brings airtight logic and technical rigor.
Debates facts while missing the room's political/cultural frame.
Tell: Flooding a stuck meeting with extra slides.
Move: Pause data and name the room's real tension in one sentence.
guard: Guards with proof & armor
Catches subtle logical inconsistencies fast.
Over-intellectualizes motives; debates bad-faith pushers.
Tell: Explaining why they're wrong instead of holding a limit.
Move: Switch from proving to a 1-sentence boundary + written trail.
bridges: Minimization (Room Analogy)
High precision across technical standards.
Treats own cultural/professional norm as universal objectivity.
Tell: 'That's just inefficient / illogical.'
Move: Rewrite one proposal into a target room's native currency.

steer: Steers to the deal
Moves teams reliably toward measurable outcomes.
Uses partnership language to funnel a room toward one outcome.
Tell: 'In the spirit of partnership, let's lock this today.'
Move: Invite genuine double-loop dissent on the goal itself.
guard: Guards with contracts & leverage
Prepares BATNA and tracks deliverables cleanly.
Treats relationships like chessboards; misses relational subtleties.
Tell: Turning every friction into a win/loss scoreboard.
Move: Step out of a zero-sum game openly without needing to win.
bridges: Minimization / Acceptance (Room Analogy)
Adapts smoothly to get cross-border deals done.
Instrumental adaptation; drops cultural curiosity once the deal closes.
Tell: Learning norms only as leverage.
Move: Build one virtual third-culture norm with zero agenda.

steer: Hesitates to steer
Surfaces marginalized voices and multiple frames.
Avoids taking the wheel; lets rooms spin in relativity.
Tell: 'Every perspective is valid—what do you all think?'
Move: Pair multi-perspectival framing with one concrete proposal.
guard: Guards by understanding motives
Sees the suffering behind difficult behavior.
Over-understands; excuses repeated covert tactics.
Tell: 'From their background, it makes sense why they did that.'
Move: Keep compassion AND enforce a written walk-away line.
bridges: Acceptance (Room Analogy)
Genuine curiosity about cultural frames.
Value paralysis or Reversal (idealizing the other culture).
Tell: Hesitating to commit; disparaging own origin culture.
Move: Run the Reversal Check and anchor one concrete commitment.

steer: Steers the dynamic transparently
Names patterns aloud tentatively; double-loop reframes.
Overestimates others' readiness; names too much too soon.
Tell: 'I notice we're in a status loop—let's redesign this.'
Move: Trim the diagnosis by 50%; land one concrete next step.
guard: Guards by naming the game
Declines covert games calmly without counter-attacking.
Naming as a subtle power move to stay one-up.
Tell: Clinical detachment that feels superior.
Move: Check Beginner's Mind before naming; stay present to real stakes.
bridges: Adaptation (Room Analogy)
Shifts frames intentionally across tribes without losing center.
Carrying too much brokerage weight (burnout).
Tell: Bridging everyone else's friction automatically.
Move: Broker by mandate or free choice; drop reflexive taxes.

steer: Changes what it is about
Dissolves binary deadlocks by questioning the premise.
Reframes to avoid a concrete decision someone needs.
Tell: 'Maybe the real question isn't A or B…'
Move: After every premise-shift, land one concrete next step.
guard: Guards with relaxed presence
Sees manipulation as a game without getting hooked.
Detachment that misses real danger or harm.
Tell: 'Alchemist's amusement' while a real boundary is crossed.
Move: Keep Safety Rule #9 and BATNA bolted to the floor.
bridges: Constructive Marginality (Room Analogy)
At home on the margins of multiple worlds; bounded by none.
Rootlessness or floating above real commitments.
Tell: Seeing every identity as a construct and committing to none.
Move: Stay fluid in perspective, concrete in commitment.

sixFields.context: Opening minutes of interviews, negotiations, or bureaucratic windows.
sixFields.harm: Rapid nodding, vocal uptalk, fidgeting, and filling silence crack demeanor and invite harder anchoring.
sixFields.remedy: Hold physical stillness, drop terminal vocal pitch, and absorb 2–3 seconds of silence.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Projecting grounded, unhurried composure without theatrical dominance.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Over-explaining or nodding quickly to signal comprehension and precision.

sixFields.context: Targeted questioning or high-stakes contract clauses.
sixFields.harm: Over-reading single gestures or cognitive load creates false-positive paranoia.
sixFields.remedy: Score only multi-cue shifts from verified baseline within 30s; treat 11+ as a focus flag, not a verdict.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Spotting friction points so you ask one cleaner diagnostic question.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Treating a sharp behavioral read as courtroom certainty.

sixFields.context: Elicitation probes planting wrong numbers, flawed summaries, or ego-baits.
sixFields.harm: Triggers an automatic reflex to correct the record and leak guarded leverage.
sixFields.remedy: Pause 1 breath, answer narrowly, or let non-material errors pass unchallenged.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Openly checking shared understanding without entrapment.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Correcting every factual or linguistic imprecision immediately.

sixFields.context: Pitching terms or navigating compliance/bureaucratic desks.
sixFields.harm: Using internal-agency logic on an external-locus gatekeeper stalls approval.
sixFields.remedy: Diagnose dominant filter + locus in the first 90 seconds and match evidence format.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Framing proposals in the listener's clearest comprehension channel.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Defaulting to dense Cognitive analysis regardless of the audience.

sixFields.context: Persuasive pitches nesting action directives inside casual clauses.
sixFields.remedy: Break vocal rhythm and restate your own decision criteria in plain nouns.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Nesting directives inside smooth, diplomatic phrasing.

sixFields.context: Closing questions or binary choices baking in an unagreed premise.
sixFields.harm: Funnels either answer toward premature commitment.
sixFields.remedy: Name the hidden premise aloud or step outside both binary options.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Offering two genuinely consented options after alignment.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Using 'when/how' presuppositions to shortcut slow debate.

sixFields.context: Mirroring sensory hot-words paired with rapid tempo or multi-part overload.
sixFields.harm: Shifts attention from critical evaluation into hurried compliance.
sixFields.remedy: Serialize questions one by one and evaluate terms against written specs.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Moderate pacing to build natural conversational flow.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Harvesting a counterpart's hot-words to steer outcomes.

sixFields.context: Combining seating/proxemics, pattern break, authority, pacing, syntax, and urgency.
sixFields.harm: Compresses judgment and forces hurried commitment.
sixFields.remedy: Break the chain at steps 2–4 or execute a zero-reason walk-away.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Designing a clear, low-friction meeting structure.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Orchestrating room/timing leverage or trying to out-manipulate a bad-faith room.

sixFields.context: Senior stakeholder reviews, fee anchoring, and adversarial interviews.
sixFields.harm: Unilateral lip raises assert covert status dominance; lip compression hides deal-killing objections behind a polite 'fine.'
sixFields.remedy: Never lecture against contempt—hand back a peer-level diagnostic question; surface lip compression neutrally without guessing the motive.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Spotting unspoken identity or structural friction early so you can address it cleanly.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Counter-lecturing with credentials when dismissed, or mind-reading the withheld objection.

sixFields.context: Scope creep, uncompensated favors, and deadline pushback.
sixFields.harm: Timed flattery hooks intellect pride to drop critical scrutiny; Pity framing pressures you into subsidizing someone else's operational deficit.
sixFields.remedy: Accept praise in two dry words and sever it from the ask; acknowledge hardship once without moving your contract terms.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Recognizing genuine competence or constraints transparently with zero attached leverage play.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Over-delivering to live up to an intellectual compliment, or rescuing a stressed counterpart at your own expense.

sixFields.context: Opening minutes of negotiations, seating/scheduling shifts, and early rate discovery.
sixFields.harm: Trivial early concessions calibrate you as compliant and trigger consistency pressure; extreme brackets bait you into revealing your true floor.
sixFields.remedy: Hold one relaxed, low-stakes boundary early to reset suggestibility; deflect extreme brackets back to concrete deliverables.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Testing mutual logistics and clarifying real market ranges openly.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Saying yes to minor inconveniences to appear cooperative, or justifying your rate against an absurdly low anchor.

sixFields.context: Rapid-fire compound questions, multi-hour bargaining sessions, and 'one last minor clause' at minute 90.
sixFields.harm: Depletes System 2 executive control so unfavorable terms feel acceptable just to close mental friction.
sixFields.remedy: Force serialization (one point at a time) and enforce a hard 90-minute no-new-commitments firewall.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Pacing complex agreements with scheduled breaks and written summaries.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Pushing through exhaustion to close a deal in one sitting, or using dense jargon to wear down pushback.

sixFields.context: Rigged conference seating, backlighting/glare, standing-over-seated posture, and exploding same-day deadlines.
sixFields.harm: Induces subtle autonomic discomfort and compresses deliberation time to force premature sign-off.
sixFields.remedy: Reclaim spatial parity casually (shift chair/camera angle) and deploy a zero-reason walk-away against artificial deadlines.
sixFields.ethicalUse: Setting comfortable, equal-footing room geometry and honest external deadlines.
sixFields.yourTemptation: Using artificial scarcity or seating geometry to tilt leverage in a competitive room.

blackStarterCodex.context: High-pressure office crunch right before an unvetted scope handoff.
blackStarterCodex.range: Appears across polished Achievers and covert pushers alike.
blackStarterCodex.harm: Hooks your Intelligence/Approval need into saying yes against your own bandwidth.
blackStarterCodex.remedy: “Thanks for saying that. I still can't take on Q3 reconciliation this week.”
blackStarterCodex.ethical: Genuine, specific appreciation with zero strings or hidden ask attached.
blackStarterCodex.temptation: Praising a colleague's expertise right before asking them to cover an awkward task.

blackStarterCodex.context: Negotiations or vendor renewals demanding same-day sign-off without data review.
blackStarterCodex.range: Common in sales, procurement, and anxious management chains.
blackStarterCodex.harm: Bypasses deliberation and forces unilateral concessions.
blackStarterCodex.remedy: “I notice we're being pushed to lock this before reviewing assumptions—I'll respond tomorrow at 10 AM.”
blackStarterCodex.ethical: Sharing a real, transparent external cutoff early so both sides can plan.
blackStarterCodex.temptation: Using 'deadline pressure' to close a debate when I feel impatient.

blackStarterCodex.context: Verbal agreements revisited later with 'That's not what we agreed.'
blackStarterCodex.range: Appears under budget stress or accountability avoidance.
blackStarterCodex.harm: Erodes confidence in your own memory and extracts unpaid rework.
blackStarterCodex.remedy: Point calmly to the 3-line confirming email; do not debate memory.
blackStarterCodex.ethical: Explicitly flagging when new material facts require renegotiating an old agreement.
blackStarterCodex.temptation: Rationalizing a missed personal commitment as 'we never locked a firm time.'
